speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask a few questions to better understand your symptoms. Can you describe the breast mass you feel? Is it tender to the touch or does it hurt?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Has this mass caused any skin changes like dimpling, redness, or nipple retraction? Also, have you noticed any changes in your nipple discharge or any swelling in the armpit area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Mammogram and Breast Ultrasound.  
Please disregard the previous advice regarding gastroenteritis, as that is unrelated to a breast mass; these imaging studies are essential to evaluate the nature of the lesion immediately.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammography shows a smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast. Biopsy reveals leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor. Based on the mammogram showing a smooth polylobulated mass and the biopsy confirming leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth, this is a benign or potentially malignant fibroblastic tumor of the breast. I recommend surgical excision with clear margins to prevent recurrence or malignant transformation.
